documents.title: eye doctor
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The eye doctor office called and I'm booked for Jan 24. They said to bring someone to drive because they might dilate and do a treatment the same day. Is that right?

documents.title: RE: eye doctor
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Yes -- dilation makes vision blurry for a few hours, so plan on a ride. If they treat the spots in your retina that day it is usually done right in the office. Neurology and urology referrals have also been sent; their offices will reach out to schedule.

documents.title: Ophthalmology Consultation
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
OPHTHALMOLOGY -- RETINA
Visit 01/24/2023

Re: Susan Strong, DOB 01/06/1989

Thank you for this referral. 34-year-old woman with newly diagnosed Von Hippel-Lindau syndrome and type 2 diabetes, intermittent blurring of the left eye.

Visual acuity: 20/20 OD, 20/20 OS. Pupils equal, no APD. IOP 15 / 16. Anterior segments quiet.
Dilated fundus exam:
OD -- normal disc, macula and vessels; no retinal angioma; no diabetic retinopathy.
OS -- two small peripheral retinal capillary hemangioblastomas (angiomas) temporally with dilated feeder vessels, no exudate, no subretinal fluid, macula flat and dry. No diabetic retinopathy.

Impression: VHL-associated retinal angiomas, left eye. No diabetic retinopathy either eye.

Procedure: after consent, laser photocoagulation was applied to both lesions in the left eye. Tolerated well.

Plan: return in one year for dilated exam, sooner for any change in vision. Diabetic eye exam satisfied for this year.

Medications reviewed: metformin, lisinopril, metoprolol succinate. Allergies: NKDA.

Retina Service

documents.title: Prior authorization - MRI abdomen
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Urology office requested MRI abdomen w/wo prior to consult. MassHealth PA submitted under our office's referral, approved. Scheduled 2/13.

reports.study: MRI abdomen with and without contrast
reports.text:
EXAM: MRI abdomen without and with IV gadolinium, renal protocol.
INDICATION: VHL, solid right renal mass on ultrasound, solitary kidney.
COMPARISON: Ultrasound 12/12/2022.
FINDINGS: Left kidney surgically absent; nephrectomy bed clear. Right kidney: 2.0 x 1.9 cm solid enhancing lesion in the interpolar cortex, T2 hyperintense, without renal vein involvement. Multiple simple cysts, largest 1.4 cm upper pole, none enhancing. No hydronephrosis. Adrenal glands normal. Pancreas normal in size and signal without cyst or mass. Liver and spleen unremarkable. No lymphadenopathy.
reports.conclusion: 2.0 cm solid enhancing right renal lesion, consistent with clear cell renal cell carcinoma in VHL. Multiple simple right renal cysts. Adrenals and pancreas unremarkable.

events.reason: Solid right renal mass, solitary kidney, VHL

documents.title: Urology Consultation
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
UROLOGY CONSULTATION -- 02/21/2023

Dear Doctor,

I saw Ms. Strong today. She is a 34-year-old with VHL, s/p left radical nephrectomy in 2020 for clear cell RCC, now with a 2.0 cm solid enhancing lesion in her solitary right kidney on MRI 2/13/23, along with simple cysts.

Allergies: NKDA. Meds: metformin, lisinopril, metoprolol.

Exam: well appearing, healed left flank incision, no CVA tenderness.
Creatinine 1.0 on your recent labs.

Assessment: VHL-associated renal tumor, 2.0 cm, solitary kidney.
Plan: For VHL renal tumors we follow with active surveillance and consider nephron-sparing treatment when the largest solid lesion reaches 3 cm. Repeat MRI abdomen in 12 months. Avoid NSAIDs given solitary kidney. She understands and agrees.

Urology

documents.title: Neurology Consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Neurology -- new consult, 3/14/2023

Reason: CNS hemangioblastomas in newly diagnosed VHL.

Ms. Strong reports intermittent frontal headaches over the past several months, a few days a week, relieved partly by acetaminophen. No vomiting, no gait trouble, no limb weakness or sensory change, no bladder symptoms. Left eye blurring was treated by retina in January.

Exam: alert, fluent. Cranial nerves intact. Strength full, reflexes 2+ and symmetric, toes down. Sensation intact. Finger-nose and heel-shin normal, tandem gait normal.

Imaging reviewed (12/14/22): left cerebellar 1.1 cm and vermian 0.6 cm hemangioblastomas without cyst or hydrocephalus; small C4 and T8 intramedullary lesions without syrinx.

Impression: Asymptomatic-appearing small hemangioblastomas; headaches not localizing and not clearly attributable to the lesions.
Plan: Observation. Repeat MRI brain in 12-18 months, sooner for new headache pattern, imbalance, weakness or numbness. Acetaminophen as needed; limit to a few days a week.

Neurology

documents.title: Psychiatry Intake
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Community Behavioral Health -- Psychiatric Evaluation
Date: 5/30/2023

Identifying: 34 y/o woman with longstanding bipolar I disorder referred by PCP to re-establish psychiatric care after several years without treatment due to lack of insurance.

She describes the illness as long-standing and has been off medication for years. Her mood has felt unsettled off treatment and she wants to be back on a mood stabilizer. No suicidal or homicidal ideation. No psychosis today.

Medical: type 2 diabetes, hypertension, Von Hippel-Lindau syndrome, h/o RCC s/p left nephrectomy, PCOS.
Meds: metformin, lisinopril, metoprolol succinate. NKDA.
Substances: never smoker, alcohol 1-2 drinks monthly, no drugs.
Family: maternal uncle with bipolar disorder.

MSE: casually dressed, cooperative, speech normal rate, mood "OK," affect full range, thought process linear, no SI/HI, insight and judgment fair.

Dx: Bipolar I disorder.
Plan: Start olanzapine 10 mg at bedtime for mood stabilization. Discussed weight gain and blood sugar effects given her diabetes; she prefers this option and will keep her PCP labs up to date. Follow up in 6 months, sooner if needed; crisis line provided.

Psychiatry

documents.title: Endocrinology Consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
ENDOCRINOLOGY
Consultation 06/13/2023

Referred for VHL with elevated plasma normetanephrine and diabetes.

HPI: Over the past six months she has gained weight, bruises easily, and her periods have been irregular. She has noticed her face getting rounder and has new acne. Diabetes diagnosed last year, on metformin. PCOS diagnosed by gyn last fall. Hypertension on lisinopril and metoprolol. Started olanzapine with psychiatry two weeks ago.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, olanzapine 10 mg nightly.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father VHL; mother type 2 diabetes and hypertension; maternal uncle bipolar disorder.
SH: never smoker; 1-2 drinks a month; works part time in an office.

Exam: BP 146/92. Central adiposity. Rounded facies with a dorsocervical fat pad. Skin thin, with purple striae across the lower abdomen. Acne on the cheeks. Thyroid normal.

Labs today: fasting glucose 126 mg/dL, A1c 7.2%.

Assessment:
1. Clinical features of Cushing syndrome -- rounded face, dorsocervical fat pad, thin skin, violaceous striae, easy bruising, weight gain.
2. VHL with elevated normetanephrine on PCP labs.
3. Type 2 diabetes, fair control.

Plan:
- 1 mg overnight dexamethasone suppression test: dexamethasone 1 mg at 11 PM, cortisol at 8 AM next morning (lab slip given).
- At follow-up in 3 months: ACTH, repeat plasma metanephrines.
- Continue current diabetes and BP regimen for now.

Endocrinology

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PREVENTIVE VISIT

34 y/o F. Interval: endocrinology 6/13 -- told she has Cushing syndrome based on exam; dexamethasone test 6/20 was not suppressed (4.1). Endo follow-up in September for ACTH and next steps. Psychiatry finally saw her 5/30 and started olanzapine 10 at night; sleeping better, feels steadier. Gyn dx PCOS last fall; cycles still irregular.

Current meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 10, metoprolol succ 50, olanzapine 10 qhs.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: still working part time. Never smoker. Rare alcohol.

ROS: headaches about the same. Bruises easily. No chest pain, dyspnea, urinary symptoms. No hypoglycemia.

EXAM
Vitals as charted.
General: well, round facies.
HEENT normal. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement.
Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear.
Abdomen soft, nontender; purple striae lower abdomen; healed left flank scar.
Pelvic: external genitalia normal, cervix without lesions, Pap with HPV collected.
Ext no edema. Skin thin, few ecchymoses on forearms.
Feet: monofilament intact, pulses 2+, no ulcers or calluses.
Neuro nonfocal.

PHQ-9: 3.

A/P
1. Preventive: Pap/HPV today. Hep B vaccine series started (Heplisav #1, #2 in one month) given diabetes. Flu shot in the fall. Exercise and diet reviewed.
2. T2DM -- A1c, CMP, urine microalbumin today. Retina exam done in January.
3. HTN -- 151/88 today, higher than her usual. Continue current meds, recheck next visit.
4. Cushing syndrome -- per endocrinology, follow-up in September.
5. VHL -- urology MRI due Feb 2024; neurology MRI due 2024. Eye exam January.
6. Bipolar I -- on olanzapine via psychiatry. Weight check at each visit.

RTC 4-5 months.

Community Behavioral Health -- Medication Follow-up
Date: 11/30/2023

34 y/o woman with bipolar I disorder, Cushing syndrome and diabetes, on olanzapine 10 mg nightly since late May.

She feels more stable than she has in years: sleeping through the night, no racing thoughts, no irritability episodes, working her usual hours. She has gained about 10 pounds since starting olanzapine and notices she is thirstier. Denies vision changes, frequent urination or genital infections.

Meds: olanzapine 10 mg qhs, metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

BP 130/85. BMI 28.
MSE: calm, euthymic, linear, no SI/HI.
Exam otherwise unremarkable.

Metabolic monitoring labs (fasting): glucose 126, A1c 6.8%, total cholesterol 210, HDL 35, triglycerides 250, LDL (calc) 130.

Assessment: Bipolar I disorder, stable on olanzapine. Weight gain on olanzapine; diabetes followed by PCP.
Plan: Continue olanzapine 10 mg qhs. Encouraged diet and activity. Copy of labs to PCP. Return in 6 months.

Psychiatry
